distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: First-layer clinical disease leaf for acute infection of the postpartum decidua/endometrium, with possible endomyometritis, parametrial, pelvic peritoneal, bacteremic, toxin-mediated, necrotizing, retained-tissue, or source-control-dependent extensions represented as mechanisms, axes, event hazards, treatment modifiers, or future subtype layers rather than disease-name qualifiers.
distillation_scope.boundary_policy: This leaf is separate from PID without postpartum uterine source, tubo-ovarian abscess as a formed adnexal abscess leaf, septic abortion, pyelonephritis/CAUTI, cesarean wound infection, mastitis, toxic shock syndrome as a systemic toxin leaf, organism-level bacteremia, retained products alone without infection, and generic sepsis. Superposition can be used when postpartum endometritis coexists with bacteremia, TSS, TOA, wound infection, pyelonephritis, or another source.
distillation_scope.ranking_note: Presentation ranking may consume postpartum timing, uterine/fundal tenderness, abdominal or pelvic pain, fever or blunted fever, malodorous or purulent lochia, cervical motion tenderness, inflammatory labs, shock physiology, and presentation ultrasound/CT evidence of endometrial thickening, endometrial collection, intrauterine gas, enlarged/subinvoluted uterus, retained products, pelvic fluid, or perihepatitis. Culture species, susceptibility, operative/pathology confirmation, final source adjudication, and treatment response remain confirmatory or non-ranking unless a post-workup mode explicitly consumes them.

latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Post-delivery decidual tissue, cervical dilation, lochia, uterine wound surfaces, cesarean hysterotomy, prolonged labor, membrane rupture, retained tissue, or uterine instrumentation create a susceptible postpartum uterine niche.
Mixed vaginal, cervical, enteric, streptococcal, enterococcal, anaerobic, and occasional resistant organisms ascend or are inoculated into the postpartum uterine cavity and decidua.
Bacterial burden triggers neutrophilic endometritis with uterine pain, fundal tenderness, endometrial thickening, increased vascularity, purulent/malodorous lochia, and inflammatory biomarkers.
Infected decidua, retained clot/tissue, and impaired uterine involution produce abnormal, purulent, cloudy, or fetid lochia and an enlarged tender uterus.
Inflammation can extend beyond decidua into myometrium, parametria, cesarean incision, pelvic cellulitis, or pelvic abscess planes, increasing pain, source-control need, and necrosis risk.

Uterine infection can drive fever, chills, tachycardia, leukocytosis, CRP/PCT rise, lactate elevation, AKI, hypotension, bacteremia, and septic shock; fever or WBC may be blunted by NSAIDs, steroids, or severe host factors.

Group A streptococcus, clostridial or gas-forming organisms, severe resistant gram-negative infection, devascularized uterus, or rapidly progressive endomyometritis can produce toxin shock, DIC, uterine necrosis, emphysematous changes, and very high mortality.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Retained tissue or devitalized uterine source-control failure
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Retained products, clot, abscess, cesarean hysterotomy defect, devitalized or necrotic uterus, embolized tissue, or inadequate drainage sustains infection despite antibiotics.

Inflammatory exudate can irritate pelvic peritoneum, adnexa, bowel, bladder, perihepatic surfaces, or surgical planes, causing guarding, free fluid, right upper quadrant pain, or Fitz-Hugh-Curtis-like perihepatitis.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Active antimicrobial coverage and source-control resolution
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Concordant broad-spectrum exposure, anaerobic and streptococcal coverage, toxin-suppressive therapy when needed, evacuation/drainage/debridement, and adequate resuscitation reshape the trajectory toward uterine source resolution.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Postpartum uterine wound surfaces and cervical access create the substrate for microbial ascent or inoculation.
Bacterial burden elicits neutrophilic decidual and endometrial inflammation.
Inflamed infected decidua can produce abnormal lochia and delayed uterine involution.
Untreated or severe endometritis can extend to myometrium and parametrial/pelvic tissues.
Uterine pathogen burden can provoke systemic inflammation even before clear imaging changes.
Deep extension increases inflammatory and bacteremic burden.
Toxin-producing or necrotizing organisms can cause abrupt shock and multiorgan injury.
Retained products, clot, or necrotic tissue sustains viable organisms.
Undrained or devitalized uterine tissue supports deeper spread.
Inflammation can extend to pelvic peritoneum and, rarely, perihepatic surfaces.
Active antimicrobial exposure lowers viable uterine microbial burden.
Control of infection allows endometrial inflammation to resolve.
Evacuation, drainage, debridement, or hysterectomy can remove persistent uterine source.
The postpartum state is the defining context for this leaf.
Timing within the puerperium changes prior and differential diagnosis.
Cesarean delivery is a major postpartum endometritis risk context.
Manual extraction, curettage, balloon tamponade, or uterine procedures can inoculate or devitalize tissue.
Endometritis classically causes uterine tenderness.
Fundal tenderness localizes uterine inflammatory pain.
Clinical and imaging endometrial inflammatory activity maps to the underlying decidual/endometrial process.
Cloudy, purulent, fetid, or otherwise abnormal lochia is a key postpartum uterine infection signal.
Anaerobic or mixed infection can make lochia malodorous.
Purulent lochia reflects uterine/cervical exudate.
Infection and retained tissue can delay normal involution.
Uterine pain often localizes to lower abdomen or suprapubic region.
Endometritis and uterine tenderness create pelvic pain.
Fever is common but can be absent in early GAS, NSAID exposure, or severe shock.
Fever, pain, hypovolemia, anemia, and sepsis raise heart rate.
Bacterial uterine infection commonly causes leukocytosis, though early severe GAS may not.
CRP tracks uterine and pelvic inflammatory burden.
Hypoperfusion and septic shock raise lactate.
Severe sepsis or TSS causes vasoplegia and hypotension.
Retained products are a persistent uterine source and mimic context.
Retained tissue, necrosis, gas, abscess, or refractory shock increases source-control pressure.
Necrotizing or ischemic infected uterus can progress to tissue necrosis.
Toxin-producing GAS can drive streptococcal TSS.
Perihepatic extension can cause RUQ pain.
Fitz-Hugh-Curtis-like perihepatitis may enhance on contrast CT.
Shock and organ injury are the major near-term mortality drivers.
TSS, DIC, and necrotizing uterine infection can rapidly become fatal.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Fundal tenderness is a more local uterine tenderness expression.
Fetid lochia is a specific subtype of abnormal lochia.
Purulent lochia is another subtype of abnormal lochia.
Fever and inflammatory sympathetic tone commonly raise heart rate.
Leukocytosis and CRP often rise together with uterine infection burden.
Hypotension and tissue hypoperfusion raise lactate.
Elevated lactate signals septic shock risk and severity.
Shock and hypoperfusion increase AKI hazard.
TSS and severe invasive GAS can produce DIC-like coagulopathy.
Infected retained tissue often requires evacuation or close source-control review.
Gas in the infected postpartum uterus can be benign after instrumentation but in systemic infection raises concern for emphysematous or necrotizing disease.
Necrotic infected uterus often requires urgent debridement or hysterectomy.
Adequate source control lowers severe outcome risk when retained tissue, abscess, or necrosis sustains infection.
Perihepatitis can produce both RUQ pain and capsular enhancement.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Gentamicin exposure requires renal dosing and toxicity monitoring.
Resistant gram-negative or enterococcal organisms can make this bundle insufficient.

side_effects.interpretation: Aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity risk depends on dose, duration, and renal reserve.

treatments.context_specific_role: Broad uterine polymicrobial and anaerobic coverage vector for uncomplicated to moderately severe postpartum endometritis when renal risk is acceptable.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Severe beta-lactam reaction changes safety path.
ESBL/AmpC/MDR organisms may not be covered.

side_effects.interpretation: Broad beta-lactam therapy can cause diarrhea or C. difficile risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Alternative broad postpartum uterine coverage vector, especially when aminoglycoside risk is undesirable and beta-lactam safety is acceptable.

treatments.treatment_name: IV piperacillin-tazobactam or broad beta-lactam coverage

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Severe sepsis increases value of broad early coverage.
Resistant gram-negative pathogens may require carbapenem or susceptibility-guided therapy.

treatments.context_specific_role: Broad severe-infection coverage lane when shock, hospital-acquired flora, wound extension, or polymicrobial pelvic infection is plausible.

treatments.treatment_name: Carbapenem for MDR gram-negative or necrotizing context

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Necrotizing endomyometritis and MDR gram-negative context increase value of reliably active broad coverage.
Susceptibility confirmation improves expected pathogen-burden reduction.

treatments.context_specific_role: Coverage lane for MDR Enterobacterales, severe healthcare-associated infection, persistent bacteremia, necrotizing uterine infection, or susceptibility-guided escalation.

treatments.treatment_name: High-dose penicillin plus clindamycin for invasive GAS/TSS context

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Toxin-mediated invasive GAS physiology requires toxin-suppressive therapy.
Pure GAS-directed therapy may not cover polymicrobial postpartum infection when organism context is unknown.

failure_modes: wrong pathogen context without broad coverage
treatments.context_specific_role: Toxin-suppression and anti-streptococcal vector when invasive GAS or streptococcal TSS is suspected or confirmed; often runs alongside broad empiric coverage until polymicrobial context is clarified.

treatments.treatment_name: Uterine evacuation for retained products or infected intrauterine material

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Evacuation helps when retained tissue or infected intrauterine material is present.
Simple evacuation may not control a necrotic uterus.

side_effects.interpretation: Evacuation can cause bleeding, perforation, or anesthesia risk depending on context.

treatments.context_specific_role: Source-control vector when presentation or early imaging suggests retained infected tissue, clot, or intrauterine material.

treatments.treatment_name: Pelvic abscess drainage or operative source control

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Benefit is largest when abscess, peritonitis, or extrauterine source is present.
Peritonitis increases urgency of operative evaluation.

treatments.context_specific_role: Source-control vector for drainable pelvic collection, parametrial abscess, surgical site extension, peritonitis, or nonresponse with suspected extrauterine focus.

treatments.treatment_name: Hysterectomy or debridement for necrotizing or refractory uterine source

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Necrotic or emphysematous uterus requires definitive source control.
Refractory shock from uterine source may improve only after definitive control.

side_effects.interpretation: Operative blood loss and dilution can lower hemoglobin.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rescue source-control vector for necrotizing endomyometritis, emphysematous uterus, devitalized uterine tissue, persistent bacteremia, or refractory shock despite active antimicrobials.

treatments.treatment_name: Sepsis resuscitation and critical care support

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hemodynamic support matters when shock is present or imminent.
Support does not sterilize the uterine source.

failure_modes: persistent shock if antibiotics or source control delayed

side_effects.interpretation: Over-resuscitation can worsen oxygenation in susceptible hosts.

treatments.context_specific_role: Physiologic support while antimicrobial and uterine/pelvic source-control vectors take effect.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Cesarean delivery after labor substantially raises postpartum endometritis risk.
Cesarean hysterotomy and labor exposure increase susceptibility.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises uterine-source prior without making cesarean a disease-name qualifier.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Long labor and ruptured membranes increase microbial ascent.
Exposure time and exams increase inoculation risk.
BV, chorioamnionitis, GBS/GAS, or genital tract dysbiosis raises uterine pathogen burden.
Anaerobic context increases value of anaerobic coverage.
Uterine manipulation or retained tissue changes source geometry.
Retained infected tissue sustains infection.
Persistent intrauterine material may require evacuation.
Hemorrhage procedures and devascularization are uterine tissue contexts.
Devascularized tissue raises necrosis and emphysematous infection hazard.
Hemorrhage lowers hemoglobin and modifies reserve.

present.trajectory_modulation: Shifts toward devitalized source-control and necrosis-risk phenotypes.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: GAS and clostridial uterine infections can be toxin-mediated and fulminant.
Toxin-producing GAS raises TSS hazard.
Clindamycin/linezolid-like toxin suppression becomes clinically important.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises shock, DIC, necrosis, and mortality hazard without hardcoding organism-level diagnosis.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: MDR organisms can make standard empiric therapy inactive.
Inactive coverage prolongs pathogen burden.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises persistent bacteremia and escalation context.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Host factors may blunt fever despite severe infection.
Lower reserve raises severe infection risk.
Comorbidity worsens severe postpartum infection outcomes.

present.trajectory_modulation: Can blunt classic signs while increasing complication hazards.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Antipyretics can mask fever.
Analgesics may reduce perceived uterine pain.

present.trajectory_modulation: Does not make disease more biologically likely, but can hide fever/pain evidence and delay recognition.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Delayed or inactive therapy sustains uterine burden.
Uncontrolled infection raises shock risk.
Delayed active coverage worsens severe outcomes.

present.trajectory_modulation: Prolongs pathogen burden until active coverage is achieved.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Uncontrolled source persists.
Retained tissue, abscess, or necrosis require source-control review.
Inadequate source control raises severe outcome risk.

present.trajectory_modulation: Source-control failure sustains infection despite antibiotics.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Breastfeeding changes medication counseling and infant monitoring.

present.trajectory_modulation: Treatment-safety context only; does not define the disease.

supportive_care: Structure postpartum timing, delivery mode, labor duration, rupture of membranes, uterine manipulation, retained tissue, postpartum hemorrhage, and uterine devascularization as context/source-control axes rather than disease-name qualifiers.

Use observed presentation evidence directly: uterine or fundal tenderness, lower abdominal or pelvic pain, fever or blunted fever, malodorous/purulent lochia, cervical motion tenderness, tachycardia, hypotension, leukocytosis, CRP/PCT, lactate, and creatinine.

Use presentation ultrasound or CT when available: endometrial thickening/heterogeneity, endometrial collection, enlarged or subinvoluted uterus, retained products, intrauterine gas, uterine wall pneumatosis, cesarean hysterotomy defect, pelvic free fluid, peritoneal inflammation, or perihepatic capsular enhancement.

Keep blood/urine/endometrial/wound culture species, susceptibility, operative findings, hysterectomy pathology, autopsy findings, final paper diagnosis, and treatment response as confirmatory or post-workup fields for presentation-only ranking.

Evaluate near neighbors fairly: TOA/formed adnexal abscess, PID, septic abortion, retained products without infection, pyelonephritis/CAUTI, cesarean wound infection, mastitis, appendicitis, cholecystitis/perihepatitis mimics, toxic shock syndrome, organism-level bacteremia, and generic sepsis.

Source control is a state variable: retained products, infected clot, abscess, uterine gas with systemic illness, devitalized or necrotic uterus, persistent bacteremia, peritonitis, or refractory shock should raise source-control need rather than adding a semantic priority label.

When invasive GAS, clostridial infection, TSS, DIC, shock, or necrotizing endomyometritis is plausible, toxin suppression, active coverage, critical care, and urgent surgical source-control review should enter the forward simulation through treatment effects and hazards.

Consider renal dosing, aminoglycoside monitoring, beta-lactam allergy, lactation/newborn exposure, hemorrhage/anemia, and postpartum thromboembolism/ICU risks as treatment-safety context axes rather than diagnostic labels.
quality_notes: Postpartum endometritis was distilled from the disease name alone; cesarean delivery, postpartum day, organism, septic shock, retained products, necrosis, and source-control states are represented as axes, mechanisms, modifiers, or event hazards.

TOA/PID/septic abortion/CAUTI/pyelonephritis/sepsis shared axes were kept generic or context-bound so postpartum endometritis does not monopolize pelvic pain, fever, pyuria, shock, abscess, or culture evidence.
No treatment priority-label fields are used.
